destinations.title: When is a canonical scalar representation admissible?
destinations.question: Which dark-energy histories satisfy the kinetic-sign requirement of the canonical scalar representation used in an excursion calculation?
destinations.summary: Checks a necessary premise of scalar reconstruction without claiming a sufficient reconstruction criterion.

systems: Dark-energy histories represented by a canonical scalar
regimes: Positive scalar density when imposing w ≥ −1
assumptions: The identity φ̇² = (1+w)ρφ applies to the proposed scalar component.
An effective coupled-dark-sector equation of state requires its own component dictionary.
conventions: For ρφ > 0, nonnegative φ̇² requires w ≥ −1; equality permits zero kinetic energy.
includes: A necessary kinetic-sign test before interpreting a scalar excursion
excludes: Sufficiency for a global scalar reconstruction
Observational validation of the proposed history

destinations.title: When does heavy-field relaxation flatten inflation?
destinations.question: When does heavy-scalar relaxation in response to inflationary energy flatten the canonically normalized inflaton potential, and when do kinetic effects or loss of moduli stabilization obstruct it?
destinations.summary: Treats flattening as a conditional mechanism whose physical effect depends on kinetic normalization and stabilization.

systems: Inflaton systems coupled to relaxing heavy scalars or moduli
targets: Shape of the canonically normalized inflaton potential
regimes: Model-specific effective descriptions with heavy-field response to inflationary energy
assumptions: Potential changes must be assessed together with kinetic effects and stabilization.
conventions: Flattening refers to the canonically normalized inflaton potential.
